Behavioural-profile clustering of Mandarin cái: complete code and results

Original hclust figures + AU/BP pvclust figures | IJCL

Reproducible research report

21 October 2026

1 Complete, editable analysis code

All statistical R code is embedded below and visible in both the .Rmd and the rendered HTML. It has not been shortened to a source(...) call. The original hclust figures and the additional AU/BP pvclust figures are generated separately.

The YAML parameter run_analysis: false means show the code without executing it again. This is the safe choice when you have already produced the output CSVs and figures. Use run_analysis: true to rerun the entire pipeline, including the corrected 2,000-replicate token bootstrap and the additional pvclust analyses.

Output images: ordinary dendrograms remain in cai_clustering_results/; new AU/BP versions are written to cai_clustering_results/optional_pvclust_AU_BP/. Both versions have PDF and 600 dpi TIFF artwork; AU/BP also has PNG previews.

1.0.1 0. Packages

# =============================================================================
# Behavioural-profile hierarchical clustering of five senses of Mandarin cai
# Reproducible analysis for the International Journal of Corpus Linguistics (IJCL)
# Code availability: [repository URL]
# =============================================================================
#
# ANALYSIS
#   - Unit of clustering: five pre-annotated senses (cai1--cai5).
#   - Input: token-level annotations, aggregated to sense-level BP proportions.
#   - Full set: predictors retained by a training-based frequency filter.
#   - Reduced set: supervised sensitivity subset selected using both
#     Cramer's V >= 0.10 and positive cforest permutation importance.
#   - Primary specification: Euclidean distance with Ward.D2 linkage.
#   - Sensitivity specifications: Euclidean-average and Canberra-average.
#   - Diagnostics: k = 2 / 3 silhouette, 2,000-replicate stratified
#     token bootstrap of distances and cluster structure, and BP contrasts.
#   - An exploratory Gap statistic is available but disabled by default;
#     no optimal-k claim is based on this five-profile diagnostic.
#
# FIGURES
#   - ALL three dendrogram specifications (Ward.D2, Euclidean-average,
#     and Canberra-average) show red rectangles for the k = 2 partition.
#   - The same format is applied to both full and reduced variable sets.
#   - Dendrograms use 8 x 6 inches, without an x-axis caption.
#   - Other diagnostic figures retain their original plotting specifications.
#   - Figures are exported as PDF and LZW-compressed TIFF (600 dpi).
#   - Optional pvclust AU/BP versions are exported to a SEPARATE directory;
#     the original hclust figures and their filenames are preserved.
#
# REPRODUCIBILITY
#   - Place 1-2000.csv in the working directory or edit INPUT_FILE.
#   - Run: source("cai_hierarchical_clustering_IJCL.R", encoding = "UTF-8")
#   - Predictor screening is based on the training partition only;
#     clustering uses all 2,000 recoded tokens.
#   - The k = 2 partition is used for interpretation, not presented as
#     the uniquely optimal solution for five aggregated sense profiles.
#   - Optional exploratory Gap results must be reported accurately if used.
#   - The final bootstrap follows bootstrap_cluster_replicates_CORRECTED(2).R:
#     identical training-derived recoding, B = 2,000, seed = 20260926.
#   - Summary confidence intervals are percentile bootstrap intervals.
# =============================================================================

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# -----------------------------
# 0. Packages
# -----------------------------
REQUIRED_PACKAGES <- c("party", "ggplot2", "pheatmap", "cluster")
missing_packages <- REQUIRED_PACKAGES[
  !vapply(REQUIRED_PACKAGES, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0L) {
  # Install only missing packages; existing installations are left unchanged.
  install.packages(missing_packages)
}
if (!all(vapply(REQUIRED_PACKAGES, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE))) {
  stop("Some required R packages are unavailable; check the installation log.")
}

# -----------------------------

1.0.2 1. Parameters

# 1. Parameters
# -----------------------------
SEED <- 159L
TEST_SHARE <- 0.20

MIN_LEVEL_N <- 20L
MIN_NONMODAL_N <- 20L

MIN_CRAMER_V <- 0.10
N_CF_TREES <- 400L
N_PERM <- 1L

N_BOOT <- 2000L
BOOTSTRAP_SEED <- 20260926L
# The Gap statistic is optional and disabled for the standard IJCL run.
# Set TRUE only when you want the complete exploratory Gap analysis,
# including any k = 1 suggestions. Do not selectively discard results.
# When enabled, its files are kept in a separate optional diagnostics folder.
RUN_GAP_ANALYSIS <- FALSE
GAP_B <- 100L

# Publication-style dendrogram settings applied to every linkage/distance.
DENDROGRAM_K_RECT <- 2L
DENDROGRAM_RECT_BORDER <- "red"

# Supplementary AU/BP-labelled dendrograms; original hclust figures stay intact.
# Multiscale pvclust resamples BP feature LEVELS, whereas N_BOOT above resamples
# annotated TOKENS within senses. Their support estimates are not interchangeable.
RUN_PVCLUST_AU_BP <- TRUE
NBOOT_PVCLUST <- 1000L
SEED_PVCLUST <- 20261021L

MUST_KEEP <- character(0)

# Sensitivity-set rule, retained from the statistical analysis script:
# AND requires both association and permutation-importance criteria.
# This avoids an apparent reduced model identical to the full model.
REDUCED_RULE <- "AND"

1.0.3 2. Input / output

# 2. Input / output
# -----------------------------
INPUT_FILE <- "1-2000.csv"

if (!file.exists(INPUT_FILE)) {
  stop("Input file not found: ", INPUT_FILE,
       ". Place it in the working directory or edit INPUT_FILE.")
}

OUT <- file.path(dirname(normalizePath(INPUT_FILE)), "cai_clustering_results")
dir.create(OUT, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

save_csv <- function(x, name) {
  utils::write.csv(
    x,
    file.path(OUT, name),
    row.names = FALSE,
    fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
  )
}

save_gg <- function(p, name, width = 9, height = 6) {
  # Display in the active plotting device (e.g., RStudio Plots).
  print(p)

  # 2) PDF
  ggplot2::ggsave(
    file.path(OUT, name),
    plot = p,
    width = width,
    height = height,
    units = "in",
    device = "pdf",
    limitsize = FALSE
  )

  # 3) TIFF, 600 dpi
  tiff_name <- sub("\\.pdf$", ".tiff", name)

  ggplot2::ggsave(
    file.path(OUT, tiff_name),
    plot = p,
    width = width,
    height = height,
    units = "in",
    device = "tiff",
    dpi = 600,
    compression = "lzw",
    limitsize = FALSE
  )

  invisible(NULL)
}

show_save_base <- function(draw, name, width = 9, height = 6) {
  # Display in the active plotting device (e.g., RStudio Plots).
  draw()

  # 2) PDF
  grDevices::pdf(
    file.path(OUT, name),
    width = width,
    height = height
  )
  draw()
  grDevices::dev.off()

  # 3) TIFF, 600 dpi
  tiff_name <- sub("\\.pdf$", ".tiff", name)

  grDevices::tiff(
    file.path(OUT, tiff_name),
    width = width,
    height = height,
    units = "in",
    res = 600,
    compression = "lzw"
  )
  draw()
  grDevices::dev.off()

  invisible(NULL)
}

show_save_heatmap <- function(heatmap, name, width, height) {
  draw <- function() {
    grid::grid.newpage()
    grid::grid.draw(heatmap$gtable)
  }

  # Display in the active plotting device (e.g., RStudio Plots).
  draw()

  # 2) PDF
  grDevices::pdf(
    file.path(OUT, name),
    width = width,
    height = height
  )
  draw()
  grDevices::dev.off()

  # 3) TIFF, 600 dpi
  tiff_name <- sub("\\.pdf$", ".tiff", name)

  grDevices::tiff(
    file.path(OUT, tiff_name),
    width = width,
    height = height,
    units = "in",
    res = 600,
    compression = "lzw"
  )
  draw()
  grDevices::dev.off()

  invisible(NULL)
}

# -----------------------------

1.0.5 4. Read and validate data

# 4. Read and validate data
# -----------------------------
raw <- utils::read.csv(
  INPUT_FILE,
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM",
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

required <- c("source_row_number", "sentence", "cai_sense", PREDICTORS)

if (!all(required %in% names(raw))) {
  stop("Missing required columns: ", paste(setdiff(required, names(raw)), collapse = ", "))
}

raw[] <- lapply(raw, function(x) trimws(as.character(x)))

if (anyNA(raw[, required]) || any(raw[, required] == "")) {
  stop("Required input columns contain missing or empty values.")
}

if (!identical(sort(unique(raw$cai_sense)), paste0("cai", 1:5))) {
  stop("cai_sense must contain exactly cai1--cai5.")
}

raw$cai_sense <- factor(raw$cai_sense, levels = paste0("cai", 1:5))

if (nrow(raw) != 2000L) {
  warning("The input does not contain exactly 2,000 rows; check the data.")
}

save_csv(as.data.frame(table(Sense = raw$cai_sense)), "01_sense_counts.csv")

# -----------------------------

1.0.6 5. Grouped train/test split

# 5. Grouped train/test split
# The split is used only to learn recoding and predictor-screening rules.
# Clustering itself uses all 2,000 tokens after recoding.
# -----------------------------
set.seed(SEED)

group_keys <- unique(raw$sentence)
group_sense <- as.character(raw$cai_sense[match(group_keys, raw$sentence)])

test_keys <- unlist(
  lapply(split(group_keys, group_sense), function(keys) {
    sample(keys, size = max(1L, round(length(keys) * TEST_SHARE)))
  }),
  use.names = FALSE
)

test_idx <- raw$sentence %in% test_keys
tr0 <- raw[!test_idx, , drop = FALSE]

# -----------------------------

1.0.7 6. Rare-level recoding learned from training data

# 6. Rare-level recoding learned from training data
# -----------------------------
maps <- list()
level_rows <- list()

for (v in PREDICTORS) {
  tab <- sort(table(tr0[[v]]), decreasing = TRUE)
  maps[[v]] <- names(tab)[tab >= MIN_LEVEL_N]

  if ("other_rare" %in% names(tab)) {
    stop("The input already contains the reserved category other_rare: ", v)
  }

  level_rows[[v]] <- data.frame(
    Variable = v,
    Level = names(tab),
    N_train = as.integer(tab),
    Proportion_train = as.numeric(tab) / nrow(tr0),
    Recoding = ifelse(names(tab) %in% maps[[v]], names(tab), "other_rare")
  )
}

save_csv(do.call(rbind, level_rows), "02_original_levels_and_recoding.csv")

recode_data <- function(d) {
  out <- d

  for (v in PREDICTORS) {
    z <- ifelse(out[[v]] %in% maps[[v]], out[[v]], "other_rare")
    out[[v]] <- factor(z, levels = c(sort(maps[[v]]), "other_rare"))
  }

  out
}

tr <- recode_data(tr0)
all_data <- recode_data(raw)

# -----------------------------

1.0.8 7. Frequency filter = FULL

# 7. Frequency filter = FULL
# -----------------------------
freq_rows <- lapply(PREDICTORS, function(v) {
  n <- sort(table(tr[[v]]), decreasing = TRUE)
  n_nonmodal <- sum(n) - max(n)

  data.frame(
    Variable = v,
    N_nonmodal = n_nonmodal,
    Modal_share = max(n) / sum(n),
    N_levels_observed = sum(n > 0),
    Frequency_pass = n_nonmodal >= MIN_NONMODAL_N && sum(n > 0) >= 2L
  )
})

freq_tbl <- do.call(rbind, freq_rows)
full_vars <- freq_tbl$Variable[freq_tbl$Frequency_pass]

if (length(full_vars) < 2L) {
  stop("Too few predictors remained after frequency filtering.")
}

model_data <- function(d, vars) {
  d[, c("cai_sense", vars), drop = FALSE]
}

# -----------------------------

1.0.9 8. REDUCED = stricter supervised sensitivity set

# 8. REDUCED = stricter supervised sensitivity set
# -----------------------------
cramers_v <- function(y, x) {
  tab <- table(y, x)
  tab <- tab[rowSums(tab) > 0, colSums(tab) > 0, drop = FALSE]

  if (min(dim(tab)) < 2L) {
    return(0)
  }

  chi <- suppressWarnings(stats::chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE)$statistic)
  as.numeric(sqrt(chi / (sum(tab) * (min(dim(tab)) - 1L))))
}

v_train <- vapply(
  full_vars,
  function(v) cramers_v(tr$cai_sense, tr[[v]]),
  numeric(1)
)

set.seed(SEED + 1L)

screen_forest <- party::cforest(
  cai_sense ~ .,
  data = model_data(tr, full_vars),
  controls = party::cforest_unbiased(
    mtry = max(2L, floor(sqrt(length(full_vars)))),
    ntree = N_CF_TREES
  )
)

set.seed(SEED + 2L)

importance_full <- party::varimp(
  screen_forest,
  conditional = FALSE,
  nperm = N_PERM
)

if (!all(full_vars %in% names(importance_full))) {
  stop("The cforest importance scores do not cover all full-set predictors.")
}

imp_train <- as.numeric(importance_full[full_vars])

if (REDUCED_RULE == "AND") {
  reduced_vars <- full_vars[
    v_train >= MIN_CRAMER_V &
      imp_train > 0
  ]
} else {
  reduced_vars <- full_vars[
    v_train >= MIN_CRAMER_V |
      imp_train > 0
  ]
}

reduced_vars <- unique(c(reduced_vars, intersect(MUST_KEEP, full_vars)))

run_reduced <- (
  length(reduced_vars) >= 2L &&
    !setequal(full_vars, reduced_vars)
)

if (!run_reduced) {
  warning(
    paste0(
      "The reduced set is insufficient or identical to the full set; ",
      "the analysis will use the full set only."
    ),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

var_sets <- list(full = full_vars)

if (run_reduced) {
  var_sets$reduced <- reduced_vars
}

if ("reduced" %in% names(var_sets)) {
  stopifnot(
    all(var_sets$reduced %in% var_sets$full),
    !setequal(var_sets$full, var_sets$reduced)
  )
}

selection_audit <- data.frame(
  Variable = full_vars,
  Cramers_V_train = unname(v_train),
  Permutation_importance_train = imp_train,
  In_full = TRUE,
  In_reduced = full_vars %in% reduced_vars
)

save_csv(selection_audit, "03_variable_selection_audit.csv")

save_csv(
  data.frame(
    Variable_set = names(var_sets),
    N_variables = vapply(var_sets, length, integer(1)),
    Variables = vapply(var_sets, paste, character(1), collapse = "; ")
  ),
  "04_variable_sets_used.csv"
)

cat("\n===== VARIABLE-SET CHECK =====\n")
cat("Full variables:", length(full_vars), "\n")
cat("Candidate reduced variables:", length(reduced_vars), "\n")
cat("Reduced actually run:", run_reduced, "\n")
cat("Removed from full:\n")
print(setdiff(full_vars, reduced_vars))

1.0.10 8b. Print / save exact predictor set and recoded levels

# 8b. Print / save exact predictor set and recoded levels
# Audit the predictor space shared with the conditional inference trees.
# -----------------------------

common_full_vars <- full_vars

common_full_levels <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(common_full_vars, function(v) {
    observed_levels <- levels(droplevels(all_data[[v]]))

    data.frame(
      Variable = v,
      Recoded_level = observed_levels,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
)

recoding_table_all <- do.call(rbind, level_rows)

common_full_recoding <- recoding_table_all[
  recoding_table_all$Variable %in% common_full_vars,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

save_csv(
  data.frame(
    Variable = common_full_vars,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  "04b_COMMON_FULL_VARIABLE_SET.csv"
)

save_csv(
  common_full_levels,
  "04c_COMMON_FULL_RECODED_LEVELS.csv"
)

save_csv(
  common_full_recoding,
  "04d_COMMON_FULL_RECODING_RECIPE.csv"
)

cat("\n===== COMMON FULL PREDICTORS AND RECODED LEVELS =====\n")
cat("N predictors:", length(common_full_vars), "\n\n")

for (v in common_full_vars) {
  lev <- levels(droplevels(all_data[[v]]))
  cat(v, ":", paste(lev, collapse = " | "), "\n")
}

if (run_reduced) {
  cat("\n===== REDUCED PREDICTORS =====\n")
  cat("N predictors:", length(reduced_vars), "\n")
  print(reduced_vars)
}

# ================================================================

1.0.11 9. Build BP proportion profiles

# 9. Build BP proportion profiles
# ================================================================

make_matrix <- function(d, vars) {
  pieces <- lapply(vars, function(v) {
    lev <- sort(unique(as.character(d[[v]])))

    m <- vapply(
      lev,
      function(z) as.numeric(as.character(d[[v]]) == z),
      numeric(nrow(d))
    )

    if (is.null(dim(m))) {
      m <- matrix(m, ncol = 1L)
    }

    colnames(m) <- paste(v, lev, sep = "::")
    m
  })

  do.call(cbind, pieces)
}

# Use the supplied response labels rather than global variables.
by_sense <- function(m, labels) {
  labels <- droplevels(factor(labels))
  sense_levels <- levels(labels)

  out <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(sense_levels, function(s) {
      colMeans(m[labels == s, , drop = FALSE])
    })
  )

  rownames(out) <- sense_levels
  colnames(out) <- colnames(m)
  out
}

# Draw a hierarchical-clustering dendrogram with the k = 2 partition
# marked by red rectangles. This helper is shared by ALL three methods.
# The rectangles visualise the selected cut without changing clustering.
save_hc <- function(hc, name, title,
                    k_rect = DENDROGRAM_K_RECT,
                    rect_border = DENDROGRAM_RECT_BORDER,
                    width = 8, height = 6) {
  draw <- function() {
    graphics::plot(
      hc,
      hang = -1,
      main = title,
      xlab = "",
      sub = ""
    )
    if (!is.null(k_rect)) {
      stats::rect.hclust(hc, k = k_rect, border = rect_border)
    }
  }
  show_save_base(draw, name, width = width, height = height)
}

profiles <- list()
clusterings <- list()
cluster_variants <- list()

for (which_set in names(var_sets)) {
  vars <- var_sets[[which_set]]

  mm <- make_matrix(all_data, vars)
  profile <- by_sense(mm, all_data$cai_sense)

  # Within each original predictor, category proportions must sum to one.
  for (v in vars) {
    cols <- startsWith(colnames(profile), paste0(v, "::"))

    stopifnot(
      any(cols),
      all(abs(rowSums(profile[, cols, drop = FALSE]) - 1) < 1e-10)
    )
  }

  profiles[[which_set]] <- profile

  save_csv(
    data.frame(
      Sense = rownames(profile),
      profile,
      check.names = FALSE
    ),
    paste0("05_profiles_", which_set, ".csv")
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Primary: Euclidean + Ward.D2
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  d_euclidean <- stats::dist(profile, method = "euclidean")

  hc_ward <- stats::hclust(
    d_euclidean,
    method = "ward.D2"
  )

  clusterings[[which_set]] <- hc_ward

  cluster_variants[[paste(which_set, "euclidean_ward", sep = "_")]] <- list(
    tree = hc_ward,
    distance = d_euclidean
  )

  # Full/reduced Ward.D2 dendrogram with the red k = 2 partition.
  # Preserve the previous output name for consistency with existing results.
  save_hc(
    hc_ward,
    paste0("Fig_01_dendrogram_euclidean_ward_2", which_set, ".pdf"),
    paste("Euclidean / Ward.D2:", which_set),
    k_rect = DENDROGRAM_K_RECT
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Sensitivity A: same Euclidean distance, average linkage
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  hc_euclidean_average <- stats::hclust(
    d_euclidean,
    method = "average"
  )

  cluster_variants[[paste(which_set, "euclidean_average", sep = "_")]] <- list(
    tree = hc_euclidean_average,
    distance = d_euclidean
  )

  # The same red k = 2 rectangles are applied to the sensitivity tree.
  save_hc(
    hc_euclidean_average,
    paste0("Fig_02_dendrogram_euclidean_average_", which_set, ".pdf"),
    paste("Euclidean / average linkage:", which_set),
    k_rect = DENDROGRAM_K_RECT
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Sensitivity B: Canberra + average linkage
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  d_canberra <- stats::dist(profile, method = "canberra")

  hc_canberra <- stats::hclust(
    d_canberra,
    method = "average"
  )

  cluster_variants[[paste(which_set, "canberra_average", sep = "_")]] <- list(
    tree = hc_canberra,
    distance = d_canberra
  )

  # Also draw red k = 2 rectangles for the Canberra-average tree.
  save_hc(
    hc_canberra,
    paste0("Fig_03_dendrogram_canberra_average_", which_set, ".pdf"),
    paste("Canberra / average linkage:", which_set),
    k_rect = DENDROGRAM_K_RECT
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Membership under illustrative k = 2 / 3
  # These illustrative partitions are not labelled as optimal.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  save_csv(
    data.frame(
      Sense = hc_ward$labels,
      Cluster_k2 = as.integer(stats::cutree(hc_ward, k = 2)[hc_ward$labels]),
      Cluster_k3 = as.integer(stats::cutree(hc_ward, k = 3)[hc_ward$labels])
    ),
    paste0("06_cluster_membership_euclidean_ward_", which_set, ".csv")
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # BP heatmap
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  hm <- pheatmap::pheatmap(
    profile,
    cluster_rows = hc_ward,
    cluster_cols = FALSE,
    color = grDevices::colorRampPalette(
      c("#f7fbff", "#6baed6", "#08306b")
    )(100),
    fontsize_col = 6,
    angle_col = 90,
    cellheight = 27,
    main = paste("BP proportions:", which_set),
    silent = TRUE
  )

  show_save_heatmap(
    hm,
    paste0("Fig_04_BP_heatmap_", which_set, ".pdf"),
    width = max(13, ncol(profile) * 0.22),
    height = 6.5
  )
}

# 10. Cross-method membership
# ================================================================
membership_all <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(cluster_variants), function(v) {
    hc <- cluster_variants[[v]]$tree

    data.frame(
      Variant = v,
      Sense = hc$labels,
      Cluster_k2 = as.integer(stats::cutree(hc, k = 2)[hc$labels]),
      Cluster_k3 = as.integer(stats::cutree(hc, k = 3)[hc$labels])
    )
  })
)

save_csv(membership_all, "07_cluster_method_sensitivity.csv")

1.0.13 11. Distance matrices

# 11. Distance matrices
# ================================================================
for (which_set in names(profiles)) {
  profile <- profiles[[which_set]]

  de <- as.matrix(stats::dist(profile, method = "euclidean"))
  dc <- as.matrix(stats::dist(profile, method = "canberra"))

  save_csv(
    data.frame(Sense = rownames(de), de, check.names = FALSE),
    paste0("08_distance_euclidean_", which_set, ".csv")
  )

  save_csv(
    data.frame(Sense = rownames(dc), dc, check.names = FALSE),
    paste0("09_distance_canberra_", which_set, ".csv")
  )
}

1.0.14 12. Optional exploratory Gap statistic (disabled by default)

# 12. Optional exploratory Gap statistic (disabled by default)
# ================================================================
# The default run skips this whole section: no Gap simulations, graphics,
# suggestion tables or CSV files are created.
# When enabled, retain ALL tested k values (including k = 1) and write
# the outputs to a clearly separated optional diagnostics directory.
# The k = 2 and k = 3 silhouette/bootstrap analyses are not affected.
# Files created by older script versions are never deleted automatically.
if (isTRUE(RUN_GAP_ANALYSIS)) {
  GAP_RELATIVE_DIR <- "optional_gap_diagnostics"
  dir.create(file.path(OUT, GAP_RELATIVE_DIR),
             recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  gap_fun <- function(x, k) {
    hc <- stats::hclust(
      stats::dist(x, method = "euclidean"),
      method = "ward.D2"
    )

    list(cluster = stats::cutree(hc, k = k))
  }

  gap_results <- list()

  for (which_set in names(profiles)) {
    which_id <- match(which_set, names(profiles))
    set.seed(SEED + 80L + which_id)

    gap <- cluster::clusGap(
      profiles[[which_set]],
      FUNcluster = gap_fun,
      K.max = 4L,
      B = GAP_B,
      d.power = 2L
    )

    gap_df <- data.frame(
      k = seq_len(nrow(gap$Tab)),
      gap$Tab,
      check.names = FALSE
    )

    gap_k <- cluster::maxSE(
      gap_df$gap,
      gap_df$SE.sim,
      method = "firstSEmax",
      SE.factor = 1
    )

    gap_results[[which_set]] <- list(
      table = gap_df,
      firstSEmax_k = gap_k
    )

    save_csv(
      gap_df,
      file.path(GAP_RELATIVE_DIR,
                paste0("10_gap_exploratory_", which_set, ".csv"))
    )

    save_csv(
      data.frame(
        Variable_set = which_set,
        Rule = c("Gap firstSEmax", "Gap global maximum"),
        Suggested_k = c(
          gap_k,
          gap_df$k[which.max(gap_df$gap)]
        )
      ),
      file.path(GAP_RELATIVE_DIR,
                paste0("11_gap_k_suggestions_", which_set, ".csv"))
    )

    gplot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
      gap_df,
      ggplot2::aes(x = k, y = gap)
    ) +
      ggplot2::geom_line() +
      ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2) +
      ggplot2::geom_errorbar(
        ggplot2::aes(
          ymin = gap - SE.sim,
          ymax = gap + SE.sim
        ),
        width = .08
      ) +
      ggplot2::geom_vline(
        xintercept = gap_k,
        linetype = "dashed"
      ) +
      ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = seq_len(nrow(gap_df))
      ) +
      ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
      ggplot2::labs(
        title = paste(
          "Exploratory gap statistic:",
          which_set,
          "(five pre-annotated senses)"
        ),
        subtitle = paste(
          "Dashed line: firstSEmax suggests k =",
          gap_k
        ),
        x = "Number of clusters",
        y = "Gap +/- simulation SE"
      )

    save_gg(
      gplot,
      file.path(GAP_RELATIVE_DIR,
                paste0("Fig_05_gap_exploratory_", which_set, ".pdf")),
      width = 8,
      height = 5
    )
  }
} else {
  message("Optional Gap analysis skipped (RUN_GAP_ANALYSIS = FALSE).")
  message("Existing Gap files from earlier runs are not deleted; ",
          "remove old 10_gap_*, 11_gap_* and Fig_05_gap_* files manually ",
          "if you want a clean output folder.")
}

1.0.16 14. Corrected stratified token bootstrap (B = 2,000)

# 14. Corrected stratified token bootstrap (B = 2,000)
# ================================================================
# This section reproduces the FINAL analysis in
# bootstrap_cluster_replicates_CORRECTED(2).R, replacing the preliminary
# B = 300 co-clustering routine (which is NOT used in the manuscript).
#
# Key properties of the final analysis:
#   - The same training-derived rare-level recoding as the main BP analysis.
#   - The exact predictor/level columns in the saved full/reduced profiles.
#   - 2,000 draws with replacement, stratified by the five annotated senses.
#   - Identical sampled token indices across all variable sets and metrics.
#   - Euclidean/Ward.D2 and Canberra/average bootstrap trees.
#   - Pairwise and core-centroid distances, with percentile CIs for contrasts.
#   - k = 2 singleton and k = 3 partition-structure stability.
#
# These analyses use all 2,000 tokens, not the holdout partition. The full
# and reduced sets have already been fixed by the preceding screening step.
# No alternative bootstrap figures or competing 300-draw results are created.

BOOT_DIR <- file.path(OUT, "cai_bootstrap_corrected")
dir.create(BOOT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

bootstrap_save_csv <- function(x, name) {
  utils::write.csv(x, file.path(BOOT_DIR, name),
                   row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
}

bootstrap_senses <- paste0("cai", 1:5)
# The main script stores cai_sense as a factor; compare its labels as character.
# This preserves the strict five-sense check without a factor/character mismatch.
stopifnot(identical(sort(unique(as.character(raw$cai_sense))), bootstrap_senses))
stopifnot(all(table(factor(raw$cai_sense, levels = bootstrap_senses)) == 400L))
stopifnot(!anyNA(raw))

# Load the main-analysis recipe; never re-estimate category thresholds here.
bootstrap_recipe <- utils::read.csv(
  file.path(OUT, "02_original_levels_and_recoding.csv"),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
stopifnot(all(c("Variable", "Level", "Recoding") %in% names(bootstrap_recipe)))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(paste(bootstrap_recipe$Variable,
                               bootstrap_recipe$Level, sep = "\r")))

# Read only the profiles produced by THIS run. In particular, do not load a
# reduced-profile CSV left over from a previous execution of another model.
bootstrap_refs <- lapply(names(profiles), function(set_name) {
  path <- file.path(OUT, paste0("05_profiles_", set_name, ".csv"))
  z <- utils::read.csv(path, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (!"Sense" %in% names(z)) stop("Missing Sense column: ", path)
  if (anyDuplicated(names(z))) stop("Duplicate profile columns: ", path)
  if (!setequal(z$Sense, bootstrap_senses) || nrow(z) != 5L) {
    stop("Expected exactly five annotated senses in: ", path)
  }
  z[match(bootstrap_senses, z$Sense), , drop = FALSE]
})
names(bootstrap_refs) <- names(profiles)

bootstrap_profile_cols <- lapply(bootstrap_refs, function(x) {
  setdiff(names(x), "Sense")
})

bootstrap_get_var <- function(col) {
  parts <- strsplit(col, "::", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
  if (length(parts) != 2L) stop("Unexpected profile column: ", col)
  parts[[1L]]
}

bootstrap_all_cols <- unique(unlist(bootstrap_profile_cols, use.names = FALSE))
bootstrap_all_vars <- unique(vapply(bootstrap_all_cols, bootstrap_get_var,
                                     character(1)))
if (!all(bootstrap_all_vars %in% names(raw))) {
  stop("Missing original predictors: ",
       paste(setdiff(bootstrap_all_vars, names(raw)), collapse = ", "))
}

# Reconstruct, independently, the main analysis's exact recoded token values.
# Levels absent from the training recipe are mapped to 'other_rare'.
bootstrap_recoded <- raw
for (v in bootstrap_all_vars) {
  sub <- bootstrap_recipe[
    bootstrap_recipe$Variable == v, c("Level", "Recoding"), drop = FALSE
  ]
  if (nrow(sub) == 0L) stop("No recoding recipe for predictor: ", v)
  mapping <- stats::setNames(as.character(sub$Recoding), as.character(sub$Level))
  z <- unname(mapping[as.character(raw[[v]])])
  z[is.na(z)] <- "other_rare"
  bootstrap_recoded[[v]] <- as.character(z)
}

# Build each set's fixed indicator matrix once; resampling reuses its rows.
bootstrap_indicators <- function(df, cols) {
  x <- vapply(cols, function(col) {
    parts <- strsplit(col, "::", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
    as.numeric(df[[parts[[1L]]]] == parts[[2L]])
  }, numeric(nrow(df)))
  if (is.null(dim(x))) x <- matrix(x, ncol = 1L)
  colnames(x) <- cols
  storage.mode(x) <- "double"
  x
}

bootstrap_Xs <- lapply(bootstrap_profile_cols, function(cols) {
  bootstrap_indicators(bootstrap_recoded, cols)
})
bootstrap_sense_idx <- lapply(bootstrap_senses, function(s) {
  which(bootstrap_recoded$cai_sense == s)
})
names(bootstrap_sense_idx) <- bootstrap_senses

bootstrap_profile_from_indices <- function(X, idx) {
  p <- do.call(rbind, lapply(idx, function(i) {
    colMeans(X[i, , drop = FALSE])
  }))
  rownames(p) <- bootstrap_senses
  colnames(p) <- colnames(X)
  p
}

# Check that the category proportions for every predictor sum to exactly one.
bootstrap_validate_profile <- function(p, set_name) {
  vars <- unique(vapply(colnames(p), bootstrap_get_var, character(1)))
  for (v in vars) {
    cols <- startsWith(colnames(p), paste0(v, "::"))
    rs <- rowSums(p[, cols, drop = FALSE])
    if (any(abs(rs - 1) > 1e-10)) {
      stop("Bootstrap profile proportions do not sum to one: ", set_name,
           " / ", v)
    }
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# Reconstructed profiles MUST reproduce the saved main BP profiles before
# bootstrapping. This also checks the exact predictor-level encoding.
bootstrap_original_profiles <- lapply(names(bootstrap_Xs), function(set_name) {
  p <- bootstrap_profile_from_indices(bootstrap_Xs[[set_name]],
                                      bootstrap_sense_idx)
  bootstrap_validate_profile(p, set_name)
  ref <- as.matrix(bootstrap_refs[[set_name]][,
              bootstrap_profile_cols[[set_name]], drop = FALSE])
  storage.mode(ref) <- "double"
  err <- max(abs(p - ref))
  cat("Bootstrap profile check [", set_name, "]: max difference = ",
      err, "\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.finite(err) || err > 1e-10) {
    stop("Bootstrap profile differs from the main BP analysis: ", set_name,
         ". Check input data, recoding, and profile files.")
  }
  p
})
names(bootstrap_original_profiles) <- names(bootstrap_Xs)

# Distances are defined independently of the hierarchical clustering.
# Pairwise: mean of the pairwise distances to the three core senses.
# Centroid: distance to the mean core profile in BP feature space.
bootstrap_get_distances <- function(p, metric) {
  core <- c("cai1", "cai2", "cai4")
  d <- as.matrix(stats::dist(p, method = metric))
  wc <- mean(d[core, core][upper.tri(d[core, core])])
  p3 <- mean(d[core, "cai3"])
  p5 <- mean(d[core, "cai5"])
  centroid <- colMeans(p[core, , drop = FALSE])
  c3 <- as.numeric(stats::dist(rbind(centroid, p["cai3", ]), method = metric))
  c5 <- as.numeric(stats::dist(rbind(centroid, p["cai5", ]), method = metric))
  c(within_pairwise = wc,
    cai3_pairwise = p3, cai5_pairwise = p5,
    cai3_centroid = c3, cai5_centroid = c5,
    gap_pair_cai3 = p3 - wc, gap_pair_cai5 = p5 - wc,
    gap_centroid_cai3 = c3 - wc, gap_centroid_cai5 = c5 - wc)
}

bootstrap_partition_key <- function(cl, labels) {
  groups <- split(labels, cl)
  groups <- vapply(groups, function(x) {
    paste(sort(x), collapse = "+")
  }, character(1))
  paste(sort(groups), collapse = "|")
}

bootstrap_singleton_k2 <- function(cl, labels) {
  groups <- split(labels, cl)
  if (sum(lengths(groups) == 1L) != 1L) return(NA_character_)
  unname(groups[[which(lengths(groups) == 1L)]])
}

# Preserve the same specification ordering as the corrected standalone code.
bootstrap_specs <- expand.grid(
  set_name = names(bootstrap_Xs),
  metric = c("euclidean", "canberra"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
bootstrap_specs$linkage <- ifelse(bootstrap_specs$metric == "euclidean",
                                   "ward.D2", "average")

bootstrap_make_record <- function(p, spec, b) {
  metric <- spec$metric
  d <- stats::dist(p, method = metric)
  hc <- stats::hclust(d, method = spec$linkage)
  k2 <- stats::cutree(hc, k = 2L)
  k3 <- stats::cutree(hc, k = 3L)
  values <- bootstrap_get_distances(p, metric)
  data.frame(bootstrap = b, variable_set = spec$set_name,
             metric = metric, linkage = spec$linkage,
             singleton_k2 = bootstrap_singleton_k2(k2, bootstrap_senses),
             partition_k2 = bootstrap_partition_key(k2, bootstrap_senses),
             partition_k3 = bootstrap_partition_key(k3, bootstrap_senses),
             as.list(values), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

# Original-sample point estimates (distinct from bootstrap means).
bootstrap_original_rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(bootstrap_specs)), function(j) {
  s <- bootstrap_specs[j, ]
  v <- bootstrap_get_distances(
    bootstrap_original_profiles[[s$set_name]], s$metric
  )
  data.frame(variable_set = s$set_name, metric = s$metric,
             linkage = s$linkage, as.list(v), check.names = FALSE)
})
bootstrap_save_csv(do.call(rbind, bootstrap_original_rows),
                   "01_original_distances.csv")

# Stratified resampling. Critically, the SAME draws are applied to each
# variable set and distance metric; seed and loop order match the final code.
set.seed(BOOTSTRAP_SEED)
bootstrap_results <- vector("list", N_BOOT * nrow(bootstrap_specs))
bootstrap_counter <- 1L
for (b in seq_len(N_BOOT)) {
  indices <- lapply(bootstrap_sense_idx, function(i) {
    sample(i, size = length(i), replace = TRUE)
  })
  sample_profiles <- lapply(names(bootstrap_Xs), function(set_name) {
    p <- bootstrap_profile_from_indices(bootstrap_Xs[[set_name]], indices)
    if (b == 1L) bootstrap_validate_profile(p, set_name)
    p
  })
  names(sample_profiles) <- names(bootstrap_Xs)
  for (j in seq_len(nrow(bootstrap_specs))) {
    sp <- bootstrap_specs[j, ]
    bootstrap_results[[bootstrap_counter]] <- bootstrap_make_record(
      sample_profiles[[sp$set_name]], sp, b
    )
    bootstrap_counter <- bootstrap_counter + 1L
  }
}
bootstrap_replicates <- do.call(rbind, bootstrap_results)
bootstrap_save_csv(bootstrap_replicates, "02_bootstrap_replicates.csv")

# Bootstrap means and percentile intervals. Do not mistake a bootstrap mean
# for the point estimate from the original (unresampled) corpus.
bootstrap_measure_cols <- names(bootstrap_get_distances(
  bootstrap_original_profiles[[1L]], "euclidean"
))
bootstrap_summary_rows <- lapply(
  split(bootstrap_replicates,
        interaction(bootstrap_replicates$variable_set,
                    bootstrap_replicates$metric, drop = TRUE)),
  function(z) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(bootstrap_measure_cols, function(measure) {
      x <- z[[measure]]
      data.frame(variable_set = z$variable_set[[1L]],
                 metric = z$metric[[1L]], linkage = z$linkage[[1L]],
                 statistic = measure, bootstrap_mean = mean(x),
                 ci_lower = unname(stats::quantile(x, 0.025)),
                 ci_upper = unname(stats::quantile(x, 0.975)))
    }))
  }
)
bootstrap_summary_table <- do.call(rbind, bootstrap_summary_rows)
bootstrap_save_csv(bootstrap_summary_table,
                   "03_bootstrap_distance_summary.csv")

bootstrap_structure_rows <- lapply(
  split(bootstrap_replicates,
        interaction(bootstrap_replicates$variable_set,
                    bootstrap_replicates$metric, drop = TRUE)),
  function(z) {
    data.frame(variable_set = z$variable_set[[1L]],
               metric = z$metric[[1L]], linkage = z$linkage[[1L]],
               k2_singleton_cai3 = mean(z$singleton_k2 == "cai3",
                                        na.rm = TRUE),
               k2_singleton_cai5 = mean(z$singleton_k2 == "cai5",
                                        na.rm = TRUE),
               k3_structure_124_3_5 = mean(z$partition_k3 ==
                                            "cai1+cai2+cai4|cai3|cai5"))
  }
)
bootstrap_save_csv(do.call(rbind, bootstrap_structure_rows),
                   "04_bootstrap_structure_summary.csv")

cat("\n=== Corrected bootstrap: FULL Euclidean / Ward.D2 ===\n")
print(subset(do.call(rbind, bootstrap_original_rows),
             variable_set == "full" & metric == "euclidean"),
      row.names = FALSE)
print(subset(bootstrap_summary_table,
             variable_set == "full" & metric == "euclidean" &
             statistic %in% c("gap_pair_cai3", "gap_pair_cai5",
                              "gap_centroid_cai3", "gap_centroid_cai5")),
      row.names = FALSE)
cat("Corrected bootstrap output: ", normalizePath(BOOT_DIR), "\n", sep = "")

1.0.17 15. BP contrast / snake plots

# 15. BP contrast / snake plots
# ================================================================
diff_plot <- function(profile, left, right, filename, title) {
  a <- colMeans(profile[left, , drop = FALSE])
  b <- colMeans(profile[right, , drop = FALSE])

  delta <- a - b
  ids <- head(order(abs(delta), decreasing = TRUE), 24)

  dd <- data.frame(
    Level = names(delta)[ids],
    Difference = unname(delta[ids])
  )

  dd <- dd[order(dd$Difference), ]
  dd$Level <- factor(dd$Level, levels = dd$Level)

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    dd,
    ggplot2::aes(x = Level, y = Difference)
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(
      yintercept = 0,
      colour = "grey60"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(
      ggplot2::aes(
        xend = Level,
        y = 0,
        yend = Difference
      )
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2) +
    ggplot2::coord_flip() +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = title,
      x = NULL,
      y = paste0(
        "P(level | ",
        paste(left, collapse = "+"),
        ") - P(level | ",
        paste(right, collapse = "+"),
        ")"
      )
    )

  save_gg(p, filename, width = 13, height = 9)

  save_csv(
    data.frame(
      Level = names(delta),
      Difference = unname(delta)
    ),
    sub("\\.pdf$", ".csv", filename)
  )
}

for (which_set in names(clusterings)) {
  hc <- clusterings[[which_set]]
  cl2 <- stats::cutree(hc, k = 2L)

  g1 <- names(cl2)[cl2 == 1L]
  g2 <- names(cl2)[cl2 == 2L]

  diff_plot(
    profiles[[which_set]],
    g1,
    g2,
    paste0(
      "Fig_08_BP_contrast_k2_",
      which_set,
      ".pdf"
    ),
    paste(
      "Illustrative BP contrast between k=2 branches:",
      which_set
    )
  )

  diff_plot(
    profiles[[which_set]],
    "cai3",
    "cai5",
    paste0(
      "Fig_09_BP_contrast_cai3_vs_cai5_",
      which_set,
      ".pdf"
    ),
    paste(
      "BP contrast: cai3 minus cai5;",
      which_set
    )
  )

  diff_plot(
    profiles[[which_set]],
    c("cai1", "cai2", "cai4"),
    c("cai3", "cai5"),
    paste0(
      "Fig_10_BP_contrast_theory_124_vs_35_",
      which_set,
      ".pdf"
    ),
    paste(
      "Theory-led BP contrast: cai1+cai2+cai4 vs cai3+cai5;",
      which_set
    )
  )
}

1.0.18 16. Final diagnostic: full vs reduced must not be duplicates

# 16. Final diagnostic: full vs reduced must not be duplicates
# ================================================================

if ("reduced" %in% names(profiles)) {
  cat("\n===== FINAL FULL / REDUCED CHECK =====\n")

  cat(
    "Profile dimensions full:",
    paste(dim(profiles[["full"]]), collapse = " x "),
    "\n"
  )

  cat(
    "Profile dimensions reduced:",
    paste(dim(profiles[["reduced"]]), collapse = " x "),
    "\n"
  )

  d_full <- as.matrix(
    stats::dist(
      profiles[["full"]],
      method = "euclidean"
    )
  )

  d_reduced <- as.matrix(
    stats::dist(
      profiles[["reduced"]],
      method = "euclidean"
    )
  )

  cat(
    "Distance matrices identical? ",
    isTRUE(
      all.equal(
        d_full,
        d_reduced,
        tolerance = 1e-12
      )
    ),
    "\n"
  )
}

1.0.19 17. Supplementary AU/BP dendrograms: pvclust

# 17. Supplementary pvclust AU/BP dendrograms (separate figures)
# ================================================================
# The regular hclust trees (Fig_01--03) were already exported above.
# This section ADDS another six figures (3 clustering methods x 2
# feature sets, when both are available); it does not replace them.
#
# Interpretation:
#   * AU = approximately unbiased support from multiscale resampling.
#   * BP = conventional bootstrap probability from pvclust.
#   * pvclust resamples the rows of t(profile), namely contextual
#     feature LEVELS, not the 2,000 annotated corpus tokens.
#   * These AU/BP support values therefore differ from the separate
#     B=2,000 sense-stratified token bootstrap results in Section 14.
#   * The seed and nboot below are reconstruction settings, not
#     verified settings from the earlier (September) AU/BP figure.
#
# Outputs:
#   OUT/optional_pvclust_AU_BP/*_RECONSTRUCTED_AU_BP.pdf
#   OUT/optional_pvclust_AU_BP/*_RECONSTRUCTED_AU_BP.tiff (600 dpi)
#   OUT/optional_pvclust_AU_BP/*_RECONSTRUCTED_AU_BP.png  (220 dpi)
#   OUT/optional_pvclust_AU_BP/*_pvclust.rds
#   OUT/optional_pvclust_AU_BP/*_edge_support.csv
#
# Disable RUN_PVCLUST_AU_BP if this optional analysis is not needed.

if (isTRUE(RUN_PVCLUST_AU_BP)) {
  if (!requireNamespace("pvclust", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("pvclust")
  }
  if (!requireNamespace("pvclust", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("Package 'pvclust' is required when RUN_PVCLUST_AU_BP=TRUE.")
  }

  AUBP_DIR <- file.path(OUT, "optional_pvclust_AU_BP")
  dir.create(AUBP_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  aubp_specs <- list(
    list(id = "Fig_01_dendrogram_euclidean_ward",
         metric = "euclidean", linkage = "ward.D2",
         label = "Euclidean / Ward.D2"),
    list(id = "Fig_02_dendrogram_euclidean_average",
         metric = "euclidean", linkage = "average",
         label = "Euclidean / average linkage"),
    list(id = "Fig_03_dendrogram_canberra_average",
         metric = "canberra", linkage = "average",
         label = "Canberra / average linkage")
  )

  aubp_draw <- function(fit, title) {
    graphics::plot(
      fit, hang = -1, main = title,
      xlab = "Pre-annotated senses", sub = ""
    )
    stats::rect.hclust(
      fit$hclust, k = DENDROGRAM_K_RECT,
      border = DENDROGRAM_RECT_BORDER
    )
  }

  aubp_save <- function(fit, stem, title) {
    # Match the reconstructed pvclust plotting script's 9 x 6 inch size.
    w <- 9
    h <- 6
    pdf_path <- file.path(AUBP_DIR, paste0(stem, ".pdf"))
    tiff_path <- file.path(AUBP_DIR, paste0(stem, ".tiff"))
    png_path <- file.path(AUBP_DIR, paste0(stem, ".png"))

    grDevices::pdf(pdf_path, width = w, height = h)
    tryCatch(aubp_draw(fit, title), finally = grDevices::dev.off())

    grDevices::tiff(
      tiff_path, width = w, height = h, units = "in",
      res = 600, compression = "lzw"
    )
    tryCatch(aubp_draw(fit, title), finally = grDevices::dev.off())

    grDevices::png(
      png_path, width = w, height = h, units = "in", res = 220
    )
    tryCatch(aubp_draw(fit, title), finally = grDevices::dev.off())

    # Keep exact support estimates and fitted model for reproducibility.
    saveRDS(fit, file.path(AUBP_DIR, paste0(stem, "_pvclust.rds")))
    if (!is.null(fit$edges)) {
      utils::write.csv(
        fit$edges,
        file.path(AUBP_DIR, paste0(stem, "_edge_support.csv")),
        row.names = TRUE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
      )
    }
  }

  aubp_summary <- list()
  for (set_name in names(profiles)) {
    # Reuse the exact in-memory BP profiles from Section 9:
    # neither the predictor set nor the category proportions are refitted.
    p <- profiles[[set_name]]
    stopifnot(nrow(p) == 5L)
    stopifnot(setequal(rownames(p), paste0("cai", 1:5)))
    p <- p[match(paste0("cai", 1:5), rownames(p)), , drop = FALSE]
    stopifnot(is.numeric(p), all(is.finite(p)))

    for (j in seq_along(aubp_specs)) {
      spec <- aubp_specs[[j]]
      aubp_seed <- SEED_PVCLUST + j +
        if (set_name == "reduced") 10L else 0L
      set.seed(aubp_seed)
      message(
        "Generating AU/BP tree: ", set_name, " / ", spec$label,
        " (nboot=", NBOOT_PVCLUST, ", seed=", aubp_seed, ")"
      )

      fit <- pvclust::pvclust(
        t(p),
        method.hclust = spec$linkage,
        method.dist = spec$metric,
        nboot = NBOOT_PVCLUST,
        parallel = FALSE
      )

      # Verify that the observed k=2 grouping matches the main hclust tree.
      reference_hc <- stats::hclust(
        stats::dist(p, method = spec$metric), method = spec$linkage
      )
      pv_k2 <- stats::cutree(fit$hclust, k = 2L)[rownames(p)]
      main_k2 <- stats::cutree(reference_hc, k = 2L)[rownames(p)]
      same_k2 <- identical(
        outer(pv_k2, pv_k2, "=="),
        outer(main_k2, main_k2, "==")
      )
      if (!same_k2) {
        warning(
          "pvclust and main hclust have different k=2 partitions for ",
          set_name, " / ", spec$label, call. = FALSE
        )
      }

      stem <- paste0(
        spec$id, "_", set_name, "_RECONSTRUCTED_AU_BP"
      )
      aubp_save(fit, stem, paste0(spec$label, ": ", set_name))

      aubp_summary[[length(aubp_summary) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
        Variable_set = set_name,
        Distance = spec$metric,
        Linkage = spec$linkage,
        N_bootstrap = NBOOT_PVCLUST,
        Seed = aubp_seed,
        Same_k2_as_main_hclust = same_k2,
        Figure_stem = stem,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
  }

  utils::write.csv(
    do.call(rbind, aubp_summary),
    file.path(AUBP_DIR, "00_pvclust_run_audit.csv"),
    row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
  )
  message("Supplementary AU/BP figures saved in: ", normalizePath(AUBP_DIR))
} else {
  message("Supplementary pvclust AU/BP figures skipped.")
}

writeLines(
  capture.output(sessionInfo()),
  file.path(OUT, "14_R_sessionInfo.txt")
)

cat("\nFinished. Output directory: ", OUT, "\n", sep = "")

2 Results, tables and figure gallery

The analysis code above is self-contained. The following tables and figures are loaded from previously saved files, so knitting with run_analysis: false does not recompute bootstrap samples. If the result folder has not yet been created, the HTML will still display all the code chapters above.

Saved results: If the results tables or figures do not appear below, place the cai_clustering_results folder beside this .Rmd. You can still read the complete R code above with run_analysis: false; set it to true only if you intentionally want to rerun all analyses.

This report includes the entire executable R analysis code above and analyses the five pre-annotated senses of Mandarin cái. It presents two separate sets of dendrograms: the original hclust figures (without node support labels) and the new pvclust figures (with AU/BP support values). Their filenames and output directories are deliberately distinct. The report also provides the behavioural-profile tables, distance analyses, corrected token bootstrap and BP contrasts.

Interpretation: The five senses, rather than individual tokens, are clustered. The displayed k = 2 rectangles are descriptive partitions, not proof that two is the uniquely optimal number of clusters. The additional pvclust AU/BP values are based on multiscale resampling of contextual-feature levels and must not be conflated with the separately reported 2,000 sense-stratified token bootstrap replicates.

2.1 Data and preprocessing

2.1.1 Sense counts

2.1.2 Full and reduced variable sets

The full analysis retains predictors passing the training-based frequency filter. The reduced sensitivity set additionally requires Cramér’s V ≥ 0.10 and positive conditional-forest permutation importance. Category recoding and predictor screening are learned on the training partition, while the sense-level BP proportions are calculated using all annotated tokens.

2.1.3 Behavioural-profile matrix

Each row represents one working sense; each feature-level column contains its within-sense proportion. Use horizontal scrolling or download the source CSV for all feature columns.

2.2 Hierarchical clustering — original figures (hclust)

The original analysis uses Euclidean distance with Ward.D2 linkage. Euclidean-average and Canberra-average provide method sensitivity checks. The red rectangles indicate the observed k = 2 partitions. These original figures contain no AU/BP annotations.

2.3 Hierarchical clustering — additional AU/BP figures (pvclust)

These figures are additional multiscale-bootstrap dendrograms, not replacements for the original plots above. Red node labels indicate approximately unbiased (AU) support, green labels indicate bootstrap probability (BP), and grey numbers denote edge identifiers; values are shown as percentages. Both figure series show the k = 2 red rectangles.

The AU/BP calculation uses pvclust with 1,000 resamples and the documented reconstruction seed (20261021, adjusted by specification). These settings reproduce the separate reconstructed workflow, not necessarily the lost original September settings. The multiscale AU/BP resampling operates across BP feature levels, whereas the corrected 2,000-draw token bootstrap in the next section resamples corpus tokens within senses.

2.4 Silhouette diagnostics

The mean silhouette widths are exploratory diagnostics for k = 2 and k = 3 on only five aggregate profiles. They should not be interpreted as proof of sharply separated natural categories.

2.5 Corrected stratified token bootstrap

The final bootstrap uses 2,000 replicates, seed 20260926, and replacement sampling separately within each of the five senses. The same sampled token indices are reused for the variable sets and distance metrics. Original-sample distance estimates are kept separate from bootstrap means and 95% percentile intervals.

2.8 Optional Gap statistic

The standard IJCL run sets RUN_GAP_ANALYSIS <- FALSE. If deliberately enabled, exploratory Gap diagnostics are stored separately under optional_gap_diagnostics/, including suggestions for k = 1. These diagnostics are not silently omitted from the interpretation of an analysis that uses them.

How to reproduce: Place cai_hierarchical_clustering_IJCL_with_AU_BP.R, this .Rmd file and 1-2000.csv in the same project directory. Click Knit in RStudio. The default run_analysis: false builds the HTML from existing analysis results without rerunning bootstrap. The pvclust AU/BP figures must already be available under optional_pvclust_AU_BP/; they cannot be reconstructed from the ordinary BP profile CSV alone. Set run_analysis: true in YAML only when you intend to rerun the entire R analysis, including the 2,000-replicate token bootstrap and the AU/BP analyses if RUN_PVCLUST_AU_BP <- TRUE. A self-contained HTML embeds the displayed images and interactive tables. When PNG previews are missing, the report can rasterise matching PDF/TIFF artwork if magick, tiff or pdftools is installed; simple hclust and BP contrast previews can also be regenerated from saved CSVs without rerunning the statistical analysis or overwriting published figures. Links to external PDF/CSV source files still require the accompanying output directory.

Repository: [repository URL] — replace this placeholder with the public archive or repository link after deposit.

2.10 Source code and figure provenance

This .Rmd is not a results-only wrapper. The full analysis is printed above as actual editable code chunks, from package loading and the frequency/ importance screens through both bootstrap methods and all plotting functions. run_analysis: false only switches off the statistical execution of those chunks; it does not hide the code. The results gallery below those chapters uses existing saved outputs. For deposited/reproducible work, the companion .R file is an exact unsegmented copy of the same analysis pipeline.
